bull.b: Additional geographic approvals and a less frequent dosing option can broaden Elfabrio’s addressable patient base and improve treatment convenience. These regulatory and product-positioning gains support longer-term market penetration beyond a single quarter’s shipment timing.

The shift to strong profitability and positive cash generation improves Protalix’s ability to fund operations and advance its pipeline internally. If sustained, this creates greater strategic flexibility and reduces dependence on external financing during development.

Low leverage and substantial liquidity provide financial resilience as Protalix supports commercialization and clinical development. The absence of outstanding debt or warrants also reduces financing pressure and preserves flexibility for investments in future growth.

bear.b: Reliance on Chiesi and uneven inventory-driven purchasing can make reported revenue difficult to predict even when underlying demand is progressing. This concentration may also limit Protalix’s control over commercialization timing and near-term cash generation.

The milestone materially boosted reported growth but does not represent recurring product sales. Future comparisons may therefore look weaker unless Elfabrio’s ongoing commercial revenue expands sufficiently to replace that contribution and demonstrate durable earnings power.

Immunogenicity and infusion-related reactions could constrain dose selection, treatment convenience and eventual efficacy for PRX-115. Until the preferred regimen is established in Phase 2, the program faces meaningful uncertainty around timing, development costs and market positioning.
